source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A guaranteed diagnosis of cancer at some point during the client's lifetime, rather than an elevated risk they can actively manage","B":"An increased lifetime risk for certain cancers, informing individualized risk management and screening decisions, though not a certainty of developing cancer","C":"A finding relevant mainly to the tested individual alone, without carrying any meaningful implications for their blood relatives","D":"Fairly little clinically relevant information at all, despite the significant family history that originally prompted the testing"}}
source_row.rationale: Positive BRCA1/BRCA2 results indicate an increased lifetime risk for certain cancers (particularly breast and ovarian), informing individualized risk management and enhanced screening decisions, though this does not guarantee the individual will develop cancer, and results may also have implications for family members who could carry the same mutation.
source_row.source_name: National Cancer Institute — BRCA Gene Testing
